maya (ML Eng): Heads-up — bringing up a converted Llama3x -> Gemma int8 build and seeing a nasty embed/perplexity drift only in long-context evals. Short contexts look fine. Suspect token fallback + kv-cache aliasing rather than quant noise.

sam (Research): Can you paste a tiny repro + numbers? quick TL;DR numbers help.

maya (ML Eng): Quick numbers from eval harness: FP16 baseline perplexity (2k context eval): 11.9 -> 12.1 (tiny). INT8 converted model: 11.9 -> 19.2 after ~1500 tokens, with repeated <unk> tokens in outputs. Short eval (<=128) INT8 perf matches FP16.

aj (Infra): That smells like tokenizer id mismatch or unknown-token fallback mapping. Did the conversion tool remap vocab ids?

maya (ML Eng): Conversion command I used:
```
convert_model \ 
  --src llama3x-fp16/ \ 
  --dst gemma-int8/ \ 
  --quant int8_static \ 
  --preserve-rotary true \ 
  --map-unk preserve \ 
  --pad-to-multiple 64
```
I also tried without --preserve-rotary and saw similar drift (slightly different failure mode).

liam (DevEx): Two quick checks: 1) tokenizer normalization (NFKC) differences can cause previously encoded tokens to split -> fallback. 2) some conversions assume unk_id==0 or 50256; if the tokenizer uses a different unk id, kv cache indices can alias. Run `python -c 'import tiktoken; print(tokenizer.encode("—"))'` vs src tokenizer.

bench-bot: smoke-run #4512 finished: int8_longctx_perp=19.2 (regression +62%), int8_shortctx_perp=12.2 (ok). logs: https://ci/rs/4512

maya (ML Eng): dug into the decoded outputs — it's literally repeating the unk token id (decoder prints <unk>) starting around token index 1200, correlates with a kv-cache overwrite window. Dumped kvcache slot id histogram and saw a spike where several distinct tokens map to the same cache index (id wrap).

sam (Research): Could be a vocab-offset or byte-to-unicode table mismatch introduced at conversion time. Are you preserving the original tokenizer file or generating a new one?

maya (ML Eng): I preserved vocab.json and merges but the conversion pipeline reassigns ids for packed layers; there is a small 'offset' applied to special tokens during packing. I think offsets + int8 packing alignment (pad-to-multiple) created a shift — unk_id ended up at a different index and some token ids exceeded kv cache capacity modulo.

aj (Infra): If it's modulo/wrap, we should see reproducible bit patterns. Can you dump the raw token id stream (pre-embedding) for a failing run? Also try running with pad-to-multiple=1 to isolate padding side-effects.

maya (ML Eng): Dump attached inline (short): `... 1187 1188 1189 0 0 0 1187 1188 1189 32000 32000 32000 ...` where 0 is expected unk for this tokenizer but converted model maps unk to 32000. That 32000 collides with kv cache index mask on our runtime (we use 16-bit slot wrap).

liam (DevEx): OK that explains the aliasing. Quick mitigation: remap unk to a high but reserved id that doesn't collide with cache mask, or expand runtime kvcache mask to 32-bit in conversion path (temporary).

maya (ML Eng): Tried two quick fixes: 1) rewrite tokenizer.json where unk_id set to 0 and regenerate tokenizer files -> still bad. 2) run conversion with `--force-vocab-offset 0` and `--pad-to-multiple 1` -> MUCH better. New eval: int8_longctx_perp=12.7 (close to FP16).

sam (Research): Nice. So root cause = conversion introduced a vocab id offset combined with packing/padding that produced ids colliding with runtime kvcache slot mask. Int8 quant didn't directly cause it but exposed the aliasing because packed tensors changed layout.

model-sre: Please capture a minimal repro script and open an infra bug. This will break customer conversions if they use custom tokenizer or different pad alignment. Also we should add a unit test in the conversion pipeline checking `max_token_id < kv_cache_slot_mask` and tokenizer.special_ids consistent.

maya (ML Eng): Will open PR. Minimal repro script (paste) below and I'm adding a regression test to eval harness.

```python
# repro_minimal.py
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
# load src tokenizer + converted tokenizer and compare id streams
src = Tokenizer.from_file('llama3x/tokenizer.json')
dst = Tokenizer.from_file('gemma_int8/tokenizer.json')
text = open('samples/long_prompt.txt').read()
ids_src = src.encode(text).ids
ids_dst = dst.encode(text).ids
print('first 200 diffs:')
for i,(a,b) in enumerate(zip(ids_src[:200], ids_dst[:200])):
    if a!=b:
        print(i, a, b)
# then run converted model with same token stream and check kvcache slot occupancy
```

liam (DevEx): Thanks — I'll add a quick check in the conversion CI job to fail on mismatched special token ids and on `max(id) & kv_mask == 0` style collisions.

maya (ML Eng): Follow-up: pushing conversion flag defaults: `--pad-to-multiple=1` and `--preserve-vocab-offsets=true` in PR #4129. Re-ran regression suite; long-context int8 failures cleared.

sam (Research): Great triage. Worth noting in the onboarding doc: always validate tokenizer special ids + kvcache assumptions after conversion, especially when quantizing/packing. I'll add a short checklist. :white_check_mark:

maya (ML Eng): Opening the PR and bug now, will ping here when CI green. Thanks all. :pray:
